question: Do radiations classified as having no detectable unconditional phylogenetic flower-colour signal still retain fine-state phylogenetic organization inside coarse colour states?
focal_frame: Among the 21 already-fixed hidden-memory opportunity clades, retain only clades whose frozen global terminal class is PROFILE_NO_PHYLOGENETIC_SIGNAL.
primary_prediction: The permutation-centered within-coarse hidden-memory effects in the focal frame are positive more often than expected under a 0.5 sign null.

primary_test.statistic: number of strictly positive centered hidden-memory effects among nonzero focal effects
primary_test.test: exact one-sided binomial sign test against p=0.5
primary_test.support_rule: median centered effect > 0 and one-sided exact sign P <= 0.05

secondary_fixed.one_sided_wilcoxon: report for continuity with the full 21-clade analysis; cannot rescue a failed sign-test primary
secondary_fixed.signalled_clades_comparison: report n, positive fraction and median hidden effect for globally signalled focal-opportunity clades descriptively only; no between-group winner test

interpretation_if_supported: A lack of detectable unconditional flower-colour signal does not imply loss of evolutionary history; fine-state history can persist cryptically inside broad phenotype classes.
interpretation_if_not_supported: The globally no-signal subgroup does not pass the frozen exact prevalence threshold, so cryptic hidden memory is reported descriptively rather than promoted as a subgroup-level inferential result.
boundaries: same source data as both component analyses; not independent replication
no reclassification of global terminal classes
Wilcoxon cannot rescue a failed exact sign-test primary
no causal ecological or molecular mechanism inferred
